```{=html}
<div class="overview">
```

::: {.notes}
About 25 seconds.
Taylor Geospatial is a nonprofit working with research and application partners on open geospatial AI.

Sources: https://taylorgeospatial.org/about-us/ and the CNG agenda.

## Related mapping and evaluation research {#research .tg-light}

```{=html}
<div class="research-overview">
<div class="research-projects"><article><h3>Features of The World</h3><p>The project extends feature mapping to roads, buildings, solar panels, and trees.</p><small>Active research</small></article>
<article><h3>Benchmarks of The World</h3><p>The project develops tools to evaluate model quality, geographic generalization, and compute requirements.</p><small>Research and evaluation tools</small></article></div>
<div class="paper"><p class="acceptance">Accepted at NeurIPS 2026</p><h3>No One Knows the State of the Art in Geospatial Foundation Models</h3>
<p>Papers use different evaluation code and methods, so reported rankings are hard to compare.</p>
<p>Performance depends on the task, sensor, and region. Strong results on selected benchmarks do not establish generalist capability.</p>
<p>We propose shared evaluation code and comparable tests across those settings.</p>
<a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12678">Corley et al. · arXiv:2605.12678</a></div>
</div>
```

::: {.notes}
About 35 seconds.
Features of The World extends feature mapping beyond fields.
Benchmarks of The World develops tools for comparing model quality, geographic generalization, and compute requirements.
Our position paper was accepted at NeurIPS 2026.
Published evaluations use different code, preprocessing, adaptation methods, and scoring implementations, so reported rankings are difficult to compare.
Model performance varies across tasks, sensors, and regions.
Strong results on a few benchmarks do not establish that a model generalizes across those settings.
We propose shared evaluation code and comparable tests to make model selection better grounded.
The paper describes a community coordination problem, including our own practices, rather than blaming individual researchers.
The slide omits numerical audit results from the older preprint while revisions are in progress.
Sources: https://taylorgeospatial.org/innovation-program/features-of-the-world/ ; https://taylorgeospatial.org/innovation-program/benchmarks-of-the-world/ ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12678.
:::

## Global FTW · 2nd edition {#ftw-preview .full}

```{=html}
<div class="image-slide"><img src="assets/stills/netherlands-2e.jpg?v=20261003" alt="Second-edition FTW field polygons in Flevoland">
<div class="image-head"><h2>Global FTW · 2nd edition</h2><p>The preview includes annual field probabilities for 2017–2025 and extracted field polygons.</p></div>
<div class="image-credit">Sentinel-2 inputs at 10 m · prediction grid at 2.5 m · selected qualitative examples · FTW / Copernicus / CDSE / Source Cooperative</div></div>
```

::: {.notes}
About 25 seconds.
Fields of The World provides open data, models, and tools for agricultural field mapping.
This is the second global map edition, separate from benchmark-dataset versioning.
The annual raster series covers 2017 through 2025.
The 2.5 m output grid comes from 10 m Sentinel-2 inputs.
Edition comparisons use the same imagery, camera, and line styling.
Archive simplification and extraction also affect the rendered boundaries.
These selected examples do not establish global accuracy.
Source: preview catalog README.
:::

## France · probability masks and polygons {#france-layers .full}

```{=html}
<div class="film"><video muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster="assets/media/france-layers-poster.jpg?v=20261003b" aria-label="Normandy, France: Irregular fields and hedgerows · 2025"><source src="assets/media/france-layers.mp4?v=20261003b" type="video/mp4"></video></div>
```

::: {.notes}
About 25 seconds. The COG stores field probability. The PMTiles archive presents extracted polygons. The raster retains low-confidence regions and soft transitions; extraction produces individual geometry. The displayed field ramp starts at 128/255, approximately 0.5. Camera: 48.88, -1.05; zoom 14; Q3. Source and capture details: MEDIA.md and assets/scenes.json.
:::

## New field blocks {#change-new-fields .paired .tg-light}

```{=html}
<p class="pair-subtitle">2018 → 2025 · annual GeoParquet outlines over same-quarter Sentinel-2 mosaics</p>
<div class="comparison-pair"><article><h3>Matopiba, Brazil</h3><video muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster="assets/media/matopiba-change-poster.jpg?v=20261003b" aria-label="Matopiba, Brazil · New rectangular field blocks"><source src="assets/media/matopiba-change.mp4?v=20261003b" type="video/mp4"></video><p>New rectangular fields across the plateau · Q3.</p></article><article><h3>Masindi, Uganda</h3><video muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster="assets/media/masindi-change-poster.jpg?v=20261003b" aria-label="Masindi, Uganda · New gridded fields"><source src="assets/media/masindi-change.mp4?v=20261003b" type="video/mp4"></video><p>A new grid of fields around existing roads · Q1.</p></article></div>
<p class="pair-source">FTW · Sentinel-2 / Copernicus / CDSE · Source Cooperative · Selected qualitative examples</p>
```

::: {.notes}
About 45 seconds. Both the imagery and the annual outlines show new field blocks. The viewer selects 2018 as the early baseline because 2017 predictions are under-detected in some regions. Matopiba uses Q3 in both years to avoid cloud gaps in the viewer’s Q1 example. No crop type or hectare total is inferred.
Source cameras, dates, and rendering details: MEDIA.md and assets/scenes.json.
:::

About 40 seconds. These examples show irrigation patterns becoming more extensive. Compare the vegetation, access tracks, and field geometry as well as the predictions. Do not infer water use or the cause of conversion from these images.
Source cameras, dates, and rendering details: MEDIA.md and assets/scenes.json.
:::

## Changes in field layout and crop activity {#change-layout-activity .paired .tg-light}

```{=html}
<p class="pair-subtitle">2018 → 2025 · annual GeoParquet outlines over same-quarter Sentinel-2 mosaics</p>
<div class="comparison-pair"><article><h3>West Bahia, Brazil</h3><video muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster="assets/media/bahia-layout-change-poster.jpg?v=20261003b" aria-label="West Bahia, Brazil · Rectangular fields replaced by center pivots"><source src="assets/media/bahia-layout-change.mp4?v=20261003b" type="video/mp4"></video><p>Rectangular fields replaced by center pivots · Q1.</p></article><article><h3>Al-Jawf, Saudi Arabia</h3><video muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster="assets/media/al-jawf-change-poster.jpg?v=20261003b" aria-label="Al-Jawf, Saudi Arabia · Fewer green center pivots in 2025"><source src="assets/media/al-jawf-change.mp4?v=20261003b" type="video/mp4"></video><p>Fewer green pivots in the later mosaic · Q3.</p></article></div>
<p class="pair-source">FTW · Sentinel-2 / Copernicus / CDSE · Source Cooperative · Selected qualitative examples</p>
```

::: {.notes}
About 40 seconds. Bahia is a layout change: the land remains agricultural. In Al-Jawf, many formerly green circles are pale in the later mosaic. This does not establish permanent abandonment or a cause. Independent annual predictions and seasonal imagery require interpretation, rather than simply equating lost polygons with lost cropland.
Source cameras, dates, and rendering details: MEDIA.md and assets/scenes.json.
:::

## COG, GeoParquet, and PMTiles {#formats .tg-light}

```{=html}
<div class="format-maps"><div><p><strong>COG</strong>Field and boundary probabilities</p><img src="assets/stills/france-field-2025.jpg?v=20261003" alt="COG field probabilities"></div><div><p><strong>PMTiles</strong>Regional summaries and field polygons</p><img src="assets/stills/pmtiles-overview.jpg?v=20261003" alt="PMTiles regional coverage map"></div></div>
<p class="format-table-label"><strong>GeoParquet</strong> · Geometry and per-field attributes</p>
<img class="format-table" src="assets/stills/geoparquet-table.jpg?v=20261003" alt="Actual GeoParquet table preview showing identifiers, geometry, bounding boxes, metrics, and scores">
<p class="format-note">The data are distributed as open files over HTTPS.</p>
```

::: {.notes}
About 30 seconds.
Cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs store probabilities, GeoParquet stores geometry and attributes, and PMTiles provides fast map browsing.
The screenshots show the preview data.
The field score is not calibrated accuracy.
The current catalog lists raster and vector collections for 2017–2025.
Source: preview catalog metadata.
:::
